aboutGame.title: What is Brushland?
paragraphs: Brushland is a cozy sandbox kingdom-builder from Transhuman Design. Instead of placing prefabs from a menu, you paint terrain tile by tile: raise mountains, carve rivers, and lay roads, then watch homes, farms, and castles emerge from the landscape.

The game is built around a relaxed single-player loop with no clock and no failure state. Villagers arrive by boat, settle into the buildings that form, and ask for bridges, work, or better views. Finished kingdoms can be recolored with 42 color looks or shared as short text codes, while the included level editor and Steam Workshop support open the door to community-made maps.

modules.name: Brushland Beginner Guide
modules.description: Learn the opening loop: paint a landscape, shape a settlement, invite villagers, and grow the first kingdom.

highlights.detail: Paint broad grassland first, then add rock and mountain shapes to frame the future settlement.
Carve rivers and waterfalls before roads so water can follow the elevation you painted.
Reserve a large flat area for the village core and connect it with a simple road spine.
Add a dock on open sea to invite the first boatload of villagers.
Watch where homes form, then answer requests for bridges, work, and scenic housing.
Refine edges and expand in small passes instead of repainting the whole map at once.

highlights.label: Docks

highlights.label: C

faq.title: Brushland FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers about Brushland's terrain painting, kingdom growth, release plans, and sharing tools.

items.question: What is Brushland?
items.answer: Brushland is a cozy sandbox kingdom-builder from Transhuman Design. You paint terrain tile by tile, then watch homes, farms, and castles grow from the landscape.

items.question: How does building work in Brushland?
items.answer: You do not place buildings from a menu. In Brushland, painted tiles react to their neighbors: roads can turn a house into a church, fields can produce a windmill, and sustained growth can raise a castle.

items.question: Can you fail in Brushland?
items.answer: No. Brushland has no clock and no failure state, so you can experiment, repaint terrain, and grow a kingdom at your own pace.

items.question: When does Brushland release?
items.answer: Brushland is planned to launch in Q2 2027, after a demo planned for Q1 2027. The launch platforms listed for Brushland are Windows, macOS, Linux, and Steam Deck.

items.question: How do you share a Brushland kingdom?
items.answer: A finished Brushland kingdom can be folded into a short text code and sent to a friend. Brushland also supports 42 color looks, Steam Workshop, and an included level editor.

items.question: Is Brushland single-player?
items.answer: Yes. Brushland is designed as a single-player experience, though finished kingdoms can be shared with friends.
